 Order
1. 1. This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual /Physical Mode).
2. Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner as well as learned Additional Standing Counsel for the State.
Perused the records.

3. This is an application under Section 482 BNSS, 2023 filed by the Petitioner for anticipatory bail,
involving offence punishable under Sections 420/34 of the Indian Penal Code read with Section 452,
506, 294, 186, 436, 511/34 of the Indian Penal Code.
4. It is stated by the learned counsel for the Petitioner that the present bail application arises out of a criminal case which had taken place in the year 1994.
He further contended that several persons of the village were arrayed as accused persons in the present case.
He further contended that many co-accused persons have been released on bail and some of them have been acquitted in the meantime.

5. Taking into consideration the aforesaid factual background, the Petitioner is directed to surrender and move for bail before the learned S.D.J.M., Kendrapara in G.R.Case No.806 of 1994 arising out of Patkura P.S.Case No.159 of 1994 within a period of three weeks from today.
In such eventuality Ramakanta @ Ramesh Chandra vs State Of Odisha .....

learned court in seisin over the matter shall do well to release the Petitioner on bail on such terms and conditions as the learned Magistrate may deem just and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case.
Violation of conditions shall entail cancellation of bail.

6. The Petitioner shall furnish a cash security of Rs.3,000/- (Rupees Three thousand) before the learned court in seisin over the matter, and shall be kept in any Nationalised Bank in interest bearing account initially for a period of one year which will be renewable from time to time till conclusion of trial and the same shall be abide by the final outcome of the trial of the case.

7. The ABLAPL is disposed of accordingly.
